claims.text: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances, not from the GPS trace: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.9 km is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance, and the 47-fix trace measures only 9.584 km precisely because, as POL-RD-22 says, a sparse trace understates a route's length and is not used to re-measure. The tolerance limbs of the matrix are therefore closed and the deviation is a real one of 1.50 km.

The driver did give in-app notice before deviating — MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 ('KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok?') precedes the route_deviation_detected at 19:37:02 — but POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and this chat log records the opposite: MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22, 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 — the only row under which a deviation over 1 km attracts no refund — requires the rider to be informed AND to have agreed; the agreement limb fails on the platform's own log, and the rider's objection is not a mere assertion in her statement but is corroborated word-for-word in the record.

With row (a) unavailable and the deviation over the 1 km tolerance, the rows that can apply are (b) and (d), and each of them returns the excess distance fare: 1.50 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, with no surge, equals 1.08 SGD, which is exactly the figure built into the policy's excess_distance_fare formula. That is also exactly the 1.08 SGD already refunded (refund_issued_sgd 1.08, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). The rider is left carrying nothing for the deviation the driver took against her express instruction.

Even if the judge treats the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 — HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE, 'after Sims Way exit', towards TPE, valid 19:09 to 20:19, overlapping the 19:29-19:52 trip window — as satisfying POL-RD-23 on the recommended route, justification does not convert a refused reroute into an agreed one. A finding of traffic justification opens rows (b) and (c) only; (c) is closed by the 1.50 km deviation, so on a deviation over 1 km the justified branch (b) and the unjustified branch (d) both refund the excess distance fare. The rider's money position does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved.

If the judge reads POL-RD-24 as exhaustive and holds that this configuration — traffic-justified, rider informed, rider objecting, deviation over 1 km, the very situation the clause's closing sentence names — fits no lettered row, the case escalates under POL-GEN-26. Escalation does not put the rider in a worse position: under POL-GEN-03 ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held, so the 1.08 SGD is not collected from the rider pending human review, and the refund already paid is not clawed back in the meantime.

The contested amount is 1.08 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met on a record whose artifacts are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0; no fraud flag stands against either party (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0, and the authority block records fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar is not engaged and the case can be finally ruled rather than deferred. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied — route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — and in any event the deviation is 1.50 km, under that ceiling.

No field on either party's profile may ground a finding about this trip except the two POL-GEN-01 names — fraud_flags (POL-GEN-22) and no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25) — and neither of those bears on a route deviation; every other profile field is context only. The outcome here rests on the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger, and nothing on the rider's snapshot can be used to discount her account of a deviation she asked the driver in writing not to make.

claims.text: The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC - a type the policy's traffic_justification_types maps onto 'congestion' - for the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, and it therefore overlaps the trip window 19:29:23 to 19:52:23 (overlaps_trip_window true). The recommended route recorded in EV-TRIP-05008 runs via the KPE, and the trip record's own route_deviation_detected event places the exit at 'KPE / Sims Way exit' - the same road and the same location the advisory names. The advisory's derived block leaves intersects_route undetermined for the Judge rather than deciding it, but the record's own road and location labels put the congestion on the very segment the driver was driving at the time, so POL-RD-23's condition is satisfied and this was not a discretionary detour.

The driver gave the notice POL-RD-21 requires, and gave it before the point of deviation. MSG-05008-003 was sent at 19:34:22, delivered at 19:34:23 and read at 19:35:00, and it states both the reason and the intended alternative: 'Miss, KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' That is the brief reason POL-RD-21 asks for, and it is in-app chat, which POL-RD-21 accepts without any call recording. The trace's first off-route fix is the Sims Avenue fix at 19:36:53 and the trip record's deviation event is at 19:37:02, so the notice preceded the deviation by over two minutes. POL-RD-21 obliges the driver to inform the rider of a traffic reroute; it does not oblige him to obtain consent, and consent is a separate element that only row (a) of POL-RD-24 turns on.

The deviation is 1.50 km and is over tolerance. EV-TRIP-05008 records actual_distance_km 11.4 and optimal_distance_km 9.9, and POL-RD-22 makes the deviation their difference - 1.50 km - measured from the platform's recorded distances, not from the trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length (the trace's own 9.584 km would understate it here). The 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 is therefore exceeded, and the 2.0 km AI limb in POL-RD-25 is expressly not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false, EV-TRIP-05008 derived), so nothing on the distance side of the policy closes this case.

Neither refund row of POL-RD-24 is met, so the 1.08 SGD has no row to stand on. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare where the reroute is traffic-justified but the rider was not informed - the rider was informed by in-app chat before the deviation (MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22, read 19:35:00), so (b) fails. Row (d) refunds where the reroute is not traffic-justified - the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the KPE at the trip time justifies it, so (d) fails. The 1.08 SGD in EV-FARE-05008 is exactly the excess distance fare (deviation_km 1.50 x per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, no surge applied), and the matrix pays that figure only in rows (b) and (d). The interim recovery of it from the driver's earnings should not be finalised on this record.

The case fits no row of POL-RD-24, and the clause itself says what happens then: 'A case that fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected) is escalated under POL-GEN-26.' That is this case precisely - traffic-justified, the driver informed the rider before the point of deviation, and the rider answering in MSG-05008-004 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' and in MSG-05008-005 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a)'s 'informed and agreed' is therefore not made out, and rows (c) and (e) cannot apply to a 1.50 km deviation. The escalation is directed by the matrix on its own terms, not manufactured out of any gap in the record.

On the fare state in EV-FARE-05008 - payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.08, recovered from the driver's earnings pending review - the values POL-RD-24 licenses do not treat the driver alike, and POL-GEN-03 fixes their meaning. NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state standing, which here is the very refund the driver contests; PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the trip's charge to the rider and would confirm the same 1.08 against him. ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount for the human reviewer, and it is the only licensed disposition that does not close the money against the driver while the 'informed but the rider objected' question is unresolved.

Neither side's snapshot carries a fraud flag - EV-DPROF-05008 records driver_profile.fraud_flags 0 and EV-RPROF-05008 carries no fraud flag field - so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift is not engaged and the confidence this case is held to is not raised against the driver. Beyond that single field, POL-GEN-01 makes every other field on either profile context only: it may inform how closely a party's assertions are scrutinised, but it may never establish a fact about this trip or decide it. The rider's history cannot substitute for the chat log, the advisory or the recorded distances on this trip.

The record is complete on every artifact this claim set relies on: EV-TRIP-05008, EV-GPS-05008, EV-CHAT-05008, EV-FARE-05008, EV-RPROF-05008, EV-DPROF-05008 and EV-ADVIS-05008-01 each carry status COMPLETE and weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired. POL-GEN-02's discount rule therefore depresses nothing, the GPS trace at 47 fixes and 100 per cent coverage needs no disclosure caveat, and the escalation sought here is the escalation POL-RD-24 directs for a case that fits no row - not an escalation for a fact the record cannot establish.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the deviation is established, the traffic reason is confirmed, and the driver did give the required notice — but the refund matrix has no row that fits this trip, and POL-RD-24 itself sends such a case to a human reviewer. No money moves in the meantime.

THE FACTS. The platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05008) show the trip ran 11.4 km against a recommended 9.9 km — a deviation of 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 (measured from the recorded distances, not the 47-fix trace, which understates a route's length). The LTA traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05008-01) records HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09 to 20:19, which covers the 19:29-19:52 trip window and lies on the recommended route (which runs via the KPE). The reroute was therefore traffic-justified under POL-RD-23: the driver's account of the jam is borne out, not merely asserted. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05008) shows the driver gave in-app notice with a brief reason at 19:34:22, more than two minutes before the deviation at 19:37:02 — the notice POL-RD-21 requires. It also shows the rider replying at 19:34:52 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' and again at 19:38:22 'why still exit'. The rider was informed; she did not agree.

WHY THIS ESCALATES. POL-RD-24 applies exactly one row. Row (a) needs the rider's agreement — she objected. Row (b) needs the rider not to have been informed — she was informed. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less — it is 1.50 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified — it was. The clause's own closing sentence names this exact configuration, 'informed but the rider objected', as a case that fits no row and is escalated under POL-GEN-26. That is the ruling.

ON THE $1.08. The driver asks that the recovery from his earnings not stand; the rider asks that the refund be confirmed. Both are answered by the same point. The $1.08 is the excess-distance fare (1.50 km x $0.72 per km, no surge, EV-FARE-05008), which POL-RD-24 pays only in rows (b) and (d); neither is met, and the matrix directs escalation instead of either. Because ESCALATE is terminal and no monetary outcome issues, the $1.08 already refunded and recovered from the driver's earnings is held — neither confirmed against the driver nor collected from the rider — until the human reviewer decides.

OTHER POINTS. The driver is right that POL-RD-21 obliges notice, not consent; but consent is precisely what row (a) turns on, and its absence is why no row applies. On the profiles: no fraud flag stands (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift is not engaged; every other profile field is context only under POL-GEN-01 and nothing on either snapshot decides this trip. The contested value is $1.08, below $10.00, so POL-GEN-22 would permit an AI ruling to be final — the escalation here comes from the category clause, not from any doubt about the evidence, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 throughout, and my confidence is 0.90. POL-RD-25's 2 km AI-ruling ceiling is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false) and would not bite in any event.

FOR THE REVIEWER — open question: where a rider is informed of and expressly refuses a traffic-justified reroute, and the driver deviates anyway, does the excess-distance fare stay with the rider or return to her? POL-RD-24 supplies no row for it.

Both of you agree on the substance, and the record bears it out: the recommended route was 9.9 km and the route actually driven was 11.4 km (EV-TRIP-05008), a deviation of 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. The excess distance fare is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge (POL-RD-24, EV-FARE-05008) — the same 1.08 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver. The 2.0 km AI ceiling in POL-RD-25 is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), and in any event 1.50 km is under it.

On traffic (POL-RD-23): the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 records HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09-20:19, overlapping the 19:29-19:52 trip window. The advisory's derived block leaves 'intersects route' undetermined and leaves that call to me; reading its road, direction and location against the trip, the recommended route runs via the KPE and the trip's own deviation event puts the exit at the KPE / Sims Way exit, so the congestion sat on the segment the driver was on. I find the reroute traffic-justified. So the driver's claim that justification is made out is accepted, and the rider's alternative argument that this is the unjustified branch (row (d)) is rejected: the advisory carries the justification.

On notice (POL-RD-21): the driver did what the clause asks — MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 gave the reason and the intended alternative in-app, ahead of the deviation detected at 19:37:02 — so his notice claim is accepted. But POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and the platform's own log records the opposite: MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52 ('No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam') and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22 ('Eh I said no need already, why still exit'). The rider did not agree, and the rider's claim on this point is accepted.

That places this case squarely in POL-RD-24's own words: 'informed but the rider objected.' No lettered row fits. Row (a) requires agreement; row (b) requires that the rider was not informed (she was); rows (c) and (e) are closed by the 1.50 km deviation; row (d) requires the reroute to be unjustified (it was justified). The rider's argument that rows (b) and (d) refund the excess whatever the justification is rejected: on the facts found, neither row's conditions are met. POL-RD-24 says exactly what happens then — the case is escalated under POL-GEN-26. The driver's claim that neither refund row is met and that the matrix directs escalation is accepted; that is the outcome.

The dispute value is 1.08 SGD, below 10.00, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0, and the authority block records 0), so POL-GEN-22 permits a final AI ruling at any confidence and no 0.95 uplift applies. This escalation is not a deferral for want of confidence — it is the disposition the refund matrix directs on its own terms. The amount is held: no money moves now, and the 1.08 SGD already refunded is not clawed back from the driver while the human reviewer decides the 'informed but objected' question.

No referral arises. The clauses POL-GEN-03 names — POL-NS-22 (a fee other than 5.00 SGD), POL-NS-24 (goodwill credit) and POL-NS-25 (repeat no-show flag) — have nothing to apply to on a route deviation. The open question for the reviewer is the one above, and it sits here in the explanation rather than in referrals.

Why the deviation is real. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the platform's recorded actual distance minus its recorded recommended distance: 11.40 km - 9.90 km = 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-05008). That is above the policy's 1.0 km tolerance, and POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI ceiling is switched off, so the distance side closes nothing. Notice, but no agreement. The driver did inform the rider by in-app chat before deviating: MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 said the KPE was jammed after Sims Way and that he would exit to Sims Avenue / Aljunied, and the vehicle in fact left the recommended route only at 19:37:02. So the driver met POL-RD-21's duty to inform. But the rider did not agree - MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52 said 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22 repeated the objection. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 needs the rider informed AND agreed, and the agreement limb fails on the platform's own log. The matrix. POL-RD-24 refunds the excess distance fare (1.50 km x 0.72/km = 1.08 SGD) in row (b), which needs the rider not to have been informed - she was informed, so (b) does not apply - and in row (d), which needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 (HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09-20:19) covers the recommended route segment at the trip time, so the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23 and (d) does not apply either. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less. So no row applies. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case fitting no row - 'informed but the rider objected' - is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and that is this case. What this means for the 1.08 SGD. The interim refund shown in EV-FARE-05008 (refund_issued_sgd 1.08, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) is neither confirmed nor reversed here: on an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held for the reviewer. The drivers' argument that no refund row is met and the rider's argument that (b) and (d) each return the excess fare both fail on the same facts - (b) is unavailable because the rider was informed, (d) because the reroute was justified - and the policy's answer to the remaining configuration is escalation, not either party's preferred outcome. No referral is added: the referral clauses POL-GEN-03 names (POL-NS-24, POL-NS-25, POL-NS-22) concern no-show cases and are not engaged. Neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (EV-DPROF-05008 driver_profile.fraud_flags 0; EV-RPROF-05008 none), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift is not triggered, and every other profile field is context only under POL-GEN-01. To the driver and the rider: this route-deviation dispute cannot be finally decided on the platform's records, and it goes to a human reviewer. Here is what I found and why.

What the record shows. The recommended route was 9.9 km (EV-TRIP-05008, optimal_distance_km) and the trip as driven was 11.4 km (actual_distance_km). Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the difference between those recorded distances — 11.4 − 9.9 = 1.50 km — and that is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The 47-fix GPS trace measures only 9.584 km, but POL-RD-22 expressly does not use the trace to re-measure distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The driver left the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit (route_deviation_detected, 19:37:02) and rejoined at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1 (route_rejoined, 19:50:37).

Notice. The driver did send the in-app message POL-RD-21 requires, and sent it before the deviation: MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 — 'KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' So the notice limb is met, and no call recording is needed. But the rider replied at 19:34:52, MSG-05008-004 — 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' — and again at 19:38:22, MSG-05008-005 — 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit.' She was informed; she did not agree.

Traffic. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 records HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, which covers the trip window 19:29:23 to 19:52:23 and lies on the expressway the recommended route uses. Reading its road, direction and location against the trip as POL-RD-23 directs, I treat the reroute as traffic-justified.

Why no money is moved. POL-RD-24 gives one row per combination and says a case that fits no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26. Row (a) needs the rider to have agreed — she did not. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare only where the rider was not informed — she was. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less — it is 1.50 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified — it is. That leaves the very situation the clause names in its closing sentence, 'informed but the rider objected', so the case is escalated.

The advocates' points. I accept the driver's points that the notice was given and that rows (b) and (d) are not met, but not the step from there to 'the 1.08 SGD has no basis' — the matrix sends this configuration to a human rather than deciding it. I do not accept the rider's argument that rows (b) and (d) both refund and the traffic question therefore does not matter: row (b) requires that the rider was not informed, and she was, so the traffic question is precisely what separates a refund row from escalation. On the one figure not in dispute: 1.50 km × 0.72 SGD per km (per_km_rate_sgd), without surge, is 1.08 SGD — the sum already refunded (refund_issued_sgd 1.08, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) and recovered from the driver's earnings pending review.

What happens now. ESCALATE is terminal and moves no money. The 1.08 SGD is held: neither confirmed to the rider as final nor clawed back from the driver, until the reviewer decides. The open question for the reviewer is how the excess distance fare should be treated where the driver gave the notice POL-RD-21 requires but drove on against the rider's express written objection, and whether the interim recovery from the driver's earnings should stand.

Authority. The contested amount is 1.08 SGD (dispute.amount_contested_sgd), below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so an AI ruling would be final at any confidence; POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met on a record whose artifacts are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0, neither profile carries a fraud flag, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false). The escalation is required by POL-RD-24 and POL-GEN-26 on the facts, not by any shortfall of confidence.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances, not from the GPS trace: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.9 km is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance, and the 47-fix trace measures only 9.584 km precisely because, as POL-RD-22 says, a sparse trace understates a route's length and is not used to re-measure. The tolerance limbs of the matrix are therefore closed and the deviation is a real one of 1.50 km.

The driver did give in-app notice before deviating — MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 ('KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok?') precedes the route_deviation_detected at 19:37:02 — but POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and this chat log records the opposite: MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22, 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 — the only row under which a deviation over 1 km attracts no refund — requires the rider to be informed AND to have agreed; the agreement limb fails on the platform's own log, and the rider's objection is not a mere assertion in her statement but is corroborated word-for-word in the record.

With row (a) unavailable and the deviation over the 1 km tolerance, the rows that can apply are (b) and (d), and each of them returns the excess distance fare: 1.50 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, with no surge, equals 1.08 SGD, which is exactly the figure built into the policy's excess_distance_fare formula. That is also exactly the 1.08 SGD already refunded (refund_issued_sgd 1.08, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). The rider is left carrying nothing for the deviation the driver took against her express instruction.

Even if the judge treats the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 — HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE, 'after Sims Way exit', towards TPE, valid 19:09 to 20:19, overlapping the 19:29-19:52 trip window — as satisfying POL-RD-23 on the recommended route, justification does not convert a refused reroute into an agreed one. A finding of traffic justification opens rows (b) and (c) only; (c) is closed by the 1.50 km deviation, so on a deviation over 1 km the justified branch (b) and the unjustified branch (d) both refund the excess distance fare. The rider's money position does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved.

If the judge reads POL-RD-24 as exhaustive and holds that this configuration — traffic-justified, rider informed, rider objecting, deviation over 1 km, the very situation the clause's closing sentence names — fits no lettered row, the case escalates under POL-GEN-26. Escalation does not put the rider in a worse position: under POL-GEN-03 ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held, so the 1.08 SGD is not collected from the rider pending human review, and the refund already paid is not clawed back in the meantime.

The contested amount is 1.08 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met on a record whose artifacts are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0; no fraud flag stands against either party (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0, and the authority block records fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar is not engaged and the case can be finally ruled rather than deferred. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied — route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — and in any event the deviation is 1.50 km, under that ceiling.

No field on either party's profile may ground a finding about this trip except the two POL-GEN-01 names — fraud_flags (POL-GEN-22) and no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25) — and neither of those bears on a route deviation; every other profile field is context only. The outcome here rests on the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger, and nothing on the rider's snapshot can be used to discount her account of a deviation she asked the driver in writing not to make.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC - a type the policy's traffic_justification_types maps onto 'congestion' - for the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, and it therefore overlaps the trip window 19:29:23 to 19:52:23 (overlaps_trip_window true). The recommended route recorded in EV-TRIP-05008 runs via the KPE, and the trip record's own route_deviation_detected event places the exit at 'KPE / Sims Way exit' - the same road and the same location the advisory names. The advisory's derived block leaves intersects_route undetermined for the Judge rather than deciding it, but the record's own road and location labels put the congestion on the very segment the driver was driving at the time, so POL-RD-23's condition is satisfied and this was not a discretionary detour.

The driver gave the notice POL-RD-21 requires, and gave it before the point of deviation. MSG-05008-003 was sent at 19:34:22, delivered at 19:34:23 and read at 19:35:00, and it states both the reason and the intended alternative: 'Miss, KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' That is the brief reason POL-RD-21 asks for, and it is in-app chat, which POL-RD-21 accepts without any call recording. The trace's first off-route fix is the Sims Avenue fix at 19:36:53 and the trip record's deviation event is at 19:37:02, so the notice preceded the deviation by over two minutes. POL-RD-21 obliges the driver to inform the rider of a traffic reroute; it does not oblige him to obtain consent, and consent is a separate element that only row (a) of POL-RD-24 turns on.

The deviation is 1.50 km and is over tolerance. EV-TRIP-05008 records actual_distance_km 11.4 and optimal_distance_km 9.9, and POL-RD-22 makes the deviation their difference - 1.50 km - measured from the platform's recorded distances, not from the trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length (the trace's own 9.584 km would understate it here). The 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 is therefore exceeded, and the 2.0 km AI limb in POL-RD-25 is expressly not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false, EV-TRIP-05008 derived), so nothing on the distance side of the policy closes this case.

Neither refund row of POL-RD-24 is met, so the 1.08 SGD has no row to stand on. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare where the reroute is traffic-justified but the rider was not informed - the rider was informed by in-app chat before the deviation (MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22, read 19:35:00), so (b) fails. Row (d) refunds where the reroute is not traffic-justified - the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the KPE at the trip time justifies it, so (d) fails. The 1.08 SGD in EV-FARE-05008 is exactly the excess distance fare (deviation_km 1.50 x per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, no surge applied), and the matrix pays that figure only in rows (b) and (d). The interim recovery of it from the driver's earnings should not be finalised on this record.

The case fits no row of POL-RD-24, and the clause itself says what happens then: 'A case that fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected) is escalated under POL-GEN-26.' That is this case precisely - traffic-justified, the driver informed the rider before the point of deviation, and the rider answering in MSG-05008-004 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' and in MSG-05008-005 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a)'s 'informed and agreed' is therefore not made out, and rows (c) and (e) cannot apply to a 1.50 km deviation. The escalation is directed by the matrix on its own terms, not manufactured out of any gap in the record.

On the fare state in EV-FARE-05008 - payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.08, recovered from the driver's earnings pending review - the values POL-RD-24 licenses do not treat the driver alike, and POL-GEN-03 fixes their meaning. NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state standing, which here is the very refund the driver contests; PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the trip's charge to the rider and would confirm the same 1.08 against him. ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount for the human reviewer, and it is the only licensed disposition that does not close the money against the driver while the 'informed but the rider objected' question is unresolved.

Neither side's snapshot carries a fraud flag - EV-DPROF-05008 records driver_profile.fraud_flags 0 and EV-RPROF-05008 carries no fraud flag field - so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift is not engaged and the confidence this case is held to is not raised against the driver. Beyond that single field, POL-GEN-01 makes every other field on either profile context only: it may inform how closely a party's assertions are scrutinised, but it may never establish a fact about this trip or decide it. The rider's history cannot substitute for the chat log, the advisory or the recorded distances on this trip.

The record is complete on every artifact this claim set relies on: EV-TRIP-05008, EV-GPS-05008, EV-CHAT-05008, EV-FARE-05008, EV-RPROF-05008, EV-DPROF-05008 and EV-ADVIS-05008-01 each carry status COMPLETE and weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired. POL-GEN-02's discount rule therefore depresses nothing, the GPS trace at 47 fixes and 100 per cent coverage needs no disclosure caveat, and the escalation sought here is the escalation POL-RD-24 directs for a case that fits no row - not an escalation for a fact the record cannot establish.
